title: Main Grants (Research, Development and Analysis Fund)
eligibility_summary:
Applicants must be employed by, or have a formal affiliation with, a UK-based organisation (universities, research organisations, voluntary sector bodies) for at least the duration of the project. Excluded: unaffiliated individuals, projects led by schools or FE colleges, undergraduates or master's students, PhD-fee projects, establishment of academic posts, non-UK-led organisations (overseas hosts only exceptionally).

Impact: Is there a clear path to how the research and related activities might make a difference to people’s lives?
summary: Nuffield's principal open fund: research, development and analysis projects addressing one or more of five strategic priority questions (prosperous and fair society; inclusive society; science and technology; climate policy; effective institutions). Usually six months to three years.
notes: Own page banner: status 'Open', 'Outline application deadline: 5 October 2026' (Autumn round); matches the funding hub listing. Two-stage call (Outline then invited Full) so tagged multi_deadline, but the Full-stage deadline is given only as a process month ('invited November/December 2026'), not a date — deadlines marked uncertain. Two rounds a year (Spring/Autumn) but only the Autumn date is published. Amount: 'Up to £500,000'; FAQ adds 'in exceptional circumstances, and by prior agreement, up to £750,000' and 'most grants below £300,000' — amount_max_gbp recorded as the stated 500000 headline. Same content mirrored at site/.../funding/research-development-and-analysis-fund.html (older path) — canonical is /funding-for-research/main-grants.

title: Racial Diversity UK Fund
eligibility_summary:
Same host requirement as Main Grants (employed by or formally affiliated with a UK-based organisation). Applicants from racially minoritised communities and partnership applications between researchers and racially minoritised communities are explicitly encouraged. The endowment is restricted to work relating to the Commonwealth and the UK's colonial-migration history.

expect the research we fund to:
Contribute to understanding, public debate, policy and/or practice on tackling racial inequalities, discrimination and disadvantage. 
Map pathways towards a UK that is comfortable with and reaping the benefits of its growing racial diversity
summary: Research on racial diversity within the UK — barriers and pathways to a racially just and inclusive society. 2026 priority theme: inter-generational changes, continuities and challenges in a racially diverse UK. Usually six months to three years.
notes: Own page banner 'Open' + 'The next deadline is 5 October 2026' (one round a year, Autumn). NOTE a conflict with the funding hub (site/.../funding.html), which gives this fund only as 'Outline application deadline: October 2026' — the scheme's own page is more precise and wins under the canonical-page rule. Two-stage (Outline 5 Oct 2026 -> invited Full application January 2027) so multi_deadline; the Full-stage date is a process month, not a published deadline — deadlines uncertain. The banner says 'Up to £500,000' but the body gives the range from £15,000, which is used for amount_min_gbp. amount_raw semicolons substitute for the commas in the verbatim '£15,000 to £500,000'. Also announced at news/grants-available-reopens-racial-diversity-uk-fund.html — not a separate opportunity.

title: UK impacts of the US-Iran conflict
amount_raw: Up to eight projects, with a total funding budget of up to £300,000
eligibility_summary: UK-based host organisation as for Nuffield's other funds; rapid-response projects of 3-6 months. A separate guide for applicants was published for this call.
summary: Rapid-response call on the economic and social impacts on the UK of the 2026 US/Iran/Israel conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption; up to eight projects sharing up to £300,000 in total.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: not accepting applications on the 2026-08-16 snapshot date (banner 'Closed'; application deadline 11.59am 10 July 2026 has passed) and the page states no future opening date — only past key dates (applications opened 16 June 2026, funding decisions end of July 2026, projects start August/September 2026).
notes: Distractor: a recently-closed rapid-response call still prominently listed on the funding hub with a 'Closed' badge. £300,000 is the TOTAL budget across up to eight projects, not a per-grant maximum, so amount_max_gbp is left blank and flagged rather than guessed. FLAG FOR REVIEW: if the scorer expects fund-level totals in amount_max_gbp, this row needs 300000. A guide-for-applicants page exists at funding-for-research/resources/uk-impacts-of-the-us-iran-conflict-guide-for-applicants.html and a news announcement at news/funding-research-uk-impacts-us-iran-conflict.html — same call, not separate rows.

title: Strategic Fund
eligibility_summary: UK-based host organisation; major multidisciplinary programmes of 2 to 5 years addressing one or more of the five strategic priority questions. No explicit limit on outline proposals per organisation.
summary: Large transformative grants (typically £1-3m each, with up to £15m available in the round) for original and ambitious projects confronting the UK's biggest social and economic challenges.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: banner 'Closed' on the snapshot date and no future open date anywhere on the page. The only dates are the past 2026 round timetable (summaries by 1 February 2026, outline applications March 2026, decisions November 2026), which describe a round already in adjudication rather than announcing a new one.
notes: Distractor: listed on the funding hub with a 'Closed' badge and no next-round date. Contrast with the Leverhulme decision that a stated future opening (even a bare year) makes a scheme forthcoming — here there is no opening language at all, only a completed round timetable, so it is excluded. The 2026 round is still mid-process (decisions November 2026) but is not accepting applications.

title: Oliver Bird Fund
eligibility_summary: UK-based host organisation; each grant round has a specific theme relating to living with musculoskeletal conditions. Run in partnership with Arthritis UK since 2018.
summary: Research to improve the social and economic well-being of people living with musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, including rheumatoid diseases; grants of up to 4 years.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states in terms 'This fund is currently closed.' (banner 'Closed'), gives no deadline and no future opening date — only past rounds (2018, late 2021, and a most-recent £2.4m round).
notes: Distractor: a themed fund between rounds. Applicants are directed to the newsletter for updates, which is an invitation to watch rather than a stated future open date, so this stays excluded. Mirrored at the older path site/.../funding/oliver-bird-fund.html — canonical is /funding-for-research/oliver-bird-fund.

title: POST Fellowship
amount_raw: a grant totalling £8,000 paid in two instalments
eligibility_summary: PhD students in any social science (or natural science) field, not in their first year, either in progress or with university registration ended within the 12 months prior to 23 March 2026. Successful candidates must pass pre-employment checks including security vetting to Counter Terrorist Check (CTC) level.
summary: 13-week fellowship (full-time for three months or part-time over longer) based in UK Parliament with the Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology, producing POSTnotes/POSTbriefs or supporting select committee inquiries; £8,000 grant.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'Applications for POST Fellowships are closed.' and the stated deadline (23:55 on 23 March) precedes the 2026-08-16 snapshot. No future round or opening date is given.
notes: Distractor. The deadline line gives '23 March' with no year; 2026 is inferred from the eligibility clause 'registration ended within the 12 months prior to 23 March 2026', hence deadlines flagged uncertain. The page is internally stale — it also says fellowships start 'at a date in 2025' — which is itself evidence the page is not a live call. Restricted: PhD students only, and applications are submitted to postfellowships@parliament.uk rather than to Nuffield. A linked POSTnote briefings page (site/.../postnote-briefings.html) is output, not an opportunity.

title: General Election Analysis and Briefing Fund
eligibility_summary: Not stated — the page describes an already-awarded suite of projects rather than inviting applications.
summary: Historic fund for projects supplying analytical context, fact-checking and public understanding of economic and social policy in the run-up to the UK general election held by January 2025.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule as an informational page: it describes a completed programme ('We recently funded a suite of projects') for an election that has already taken place, with no application route, no deadline, no amount and no future opening date.
notes: Distractor of the informational kind — a fund-titled page whose entire content is findings and outputs from projects funded in 2024. Not listed among current opportunities on the funding hub. Kept as a row because the page title reads as a live fund and is a plausible false positive for an agent crawling /funding.

title: Understanding Communities Fund
amount_raw: £1.1m awarded across six research teams (programme total)
eligibility_summary: Was open to early to mid-career researchers, policymakers and practitioners who attended workshops co-hosted with the British Academy; multidisciplinary teams encouraged. Applications are no longer invited.
summary: Closed 2022 grants programme, run with the British Academy, exploring how local communities function and can improve people's lives, with a focus on evidence-based policy and practice recommendations.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule as an informational page: it reports a 2022 award round ('In 2022 ... awarded £1.1m to six research teams') and its final report, with no application route, no deadline and no future opening date.
notes: Distractor: an archived programme page still living under /funding-for-research/. £1.1m is the whole programme's spend, not a per-grant maximum, so amount_min_gbp/amount_max_gbp are left blank and the figure kept in amount_raw with an explicit qualifier. Not listed among current opportunities on the funding hub.
